Four settings decide whether this app can actually wake you. Each one is explained before Android asks you anything.

The alarm runs as a notification-backed service. Without the notification permission it will still ring at full volume, but the screen with the maths problem may not appear on its own — you would have to open the app to stop it.\n\nNext you will see Android’s own permission dialog.
Let the alarm fire on time

An alarm clock needs to fire at an exact minute, not “sometime soon”. If “Alarms & reminders” is off for this app, nothing can be scheduled at all and no alarm will ever ring.\n\nThe button below opens that setting.
Let the alarm take over the screen

This is what puts the keypad in front of you over the lock screen at 6am instead of a notification you have to find. Android 14 restricted it to alarm and calling apps; an alarm clock is the allowed case.\n\nWithout it the alarm still rings — you would just have to open it from the shade.
Stop the system killing the alarm

This is the one that matters most. Android’s battery optimiser, and your phone manufacturer’s own one on top of it, can freeze this app overnight so the alarm never fires — silently, with nothing to see in the morning.
This app is exempt from battery optimisation.
This app is still being battery-optimised. An alarm may not fire.
Ask Android to stop optimising this app
Android’s own optimiser can delay or block an app that has been idle for hours. An alarm clock is one of the few cases where turning it off is the right answer.
Open your phone’s own battery settings
This phone does not expose that screen, so follow the steps below by hand in Settings.

Security app → Permissions → Autostart → turn Math Alarm on.\nSettings → Apps → Math Alarm → Battery saver → No restrictions.\nIn Recents, pull the app card down and tap the lock so it is not cleared.
Settings → Battery → App battery management → Math Alarm → Allow background running.\nPhone Manager → Privacy permissions → Startup manager → turn Math Alarm on.\nLock the app card in Recents.
Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management → Math Alarm → Allow.\niManager → App manager → Autostart → turn Math Alarm on.\nSettings → More settings → Applications → Autostart.
Settings → Battery → App launch → Math Alarm → Manage manually, and switch all three options on.\nPhone Manager → Protected apps → add Math Alarm.

Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → make sure Math Alarm is not in “Sleeping” or “Deep sleeping” apps.\nSettings → Apps → Math Alarm → Battery → Unrestricted.\nTurn off “Put unused apps to sleep”.
Settings → Apps → Math Alarm → Battery → Unrestricted.\nIf your phone has any “autostart”, “background running” or “protected apps” list, add Math Alarm to it.
